paraphrase_notes: OSHA requires hazard assessment, appropriate PPE selection/communication and training where covered hazards necessitate PPE.
applicability_notes: General-industry Subpart I context; exact live-event task/site requirements still depend on the controlling workplace.
required_qualifier: Apply only where the cited OSHA provisions govern; employer/site hazard assessment controls actual PPE selection.

paraphrase_notes: Protective helmets are required for affected employees where there is potential head injury from falling objects.
applicability_notes: Do not convert venue height, rigging presence or a generic stagehand job title into an automatic national hard-hat rule absent the applicable hazard/site requirement.
required_qualifier: Where falling-object head hazards and the applicable workplace rule require head protection.

paraphrase_notes: Appropriate eye/face protection is required when covered eye/face hazards are present.
required_qualifier: When the actual task exposes the worker to a covered eye/face hazard.

paraphrase_notes: Hand-protection selection is based on task, conditions and identified hazards.
applicability_notes: Does not support a universal glove-for-every-stagehand-task rule.
required_qualifier: Use appropriate hand protection when actual hazards and the controlling workplace process require it.

paraphrase_notes: Occupational-noise controls and hearing-protection obligations depend on measured/covered exposure and applicable program requirements.
applicability_notes: The course should not infer legal exposure solely from concert/venue type.
required_qualifier: Actual exposure and applicable employer program control the requirement.

paraphrase_notes: Supports the general principle that PPE selection follows workplace hazard assessment; it does not itself establish a universal high-visibility-apparel requirement for all live-event vehicle-traffic areas.
applicability_notes: Employer/site/task and any separately applicable standard or local rule control actual high-visibility requirements.
required_qualifier: High-visibility apparel is site/task/employer controlled unless a separately applicable rule governs the specific work context.

paraphrase_notes: Package 21 correctly identifies PPE as contextual but incorrectly associates high-visibility apparel with 1910.135. Matrix review records preserve that correction.
applicability_notes: Historical internal audit only; not final external evidence for high-visibility apparel.
required_qualifier: Do not reuse the 1910.135 high-visibility attribution.

support_locator: Module 3 qualification and educational/union source family
paraphrase_notes: Package 21 corroborates the distinction between show clothing convention and PPE, but final claim-level external support should retain exact local/production examples rather than treating the internal audit as controlling evidence.
applicability_notes: Dress expectations vary by production, venue, employer and role.
required_qualifier: Show blacks are production-specific clothing direction, not a universal PPE category.

paraphrase_notes: Package 21 supports clear/brief confirmation as a recurring practice while expressly rejecting one universal vocabulary.
applicability_notes: Exact phrases, radio etiquette and command vocabulary vary by production/site/employer/local.
required_qualifier: Examples are not universal commands; follow the current call's protocol.

paraphrase_notes: Supports structured reporting through steward/department authority but does not prescribe Crew Blueprint's example radio phrases.
applicability_notes: Local 101 rules are local examples, not national language standards.
required_qualifier: Local rules are contextual examples only.

paraphrase_notes: Exit routes must be free and unobstructed where the standard applies.
applicability_notes: Separate accessibility, fire-code, public-event and AHJ requirements can also apply and are not replaced by this workplace baseline.
required_qualifier: Where OSHA general-industry exit-route requirements apply.

paraphrase_notes: Supports fatigue/work-demand as a risk-management concern but does not prescribe Crew Blueprint's exact communication or break-response language.
applicability_notes: Exact break/rest/work rules remain employer/CBA/jurisdiction specific.
required_qualifier: Treat the response sequence as Crew Blueprint framing within the controlling work/break process.

paraphrase_notes: Internal audit identifies fatigue as supported while rejecting absolute comparative claims about load-out danger.
applicability_notes: Internal synthesis; underlying human-factors sources remain preferable for final external claims.
required_qualifier: Do not state that load-out is universally more dangerous than load-in.
